AUSTIN, Texas (KEYE)  —
Nearly 30,000 pounds of raw beef imported from Argentina and sold in Texas and Florida
is under recall,
according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, as questions swirl around the beef. And a string of food recalls issued this summer grows.
The beef recall notice points to missed import re-inspections as the cause, but the USDA’s Food Safety and Inspection Service classified the recalled beef as a Class I health hazard, the agency’s highest risk category. The recall notice did not mention any specific contaminants.
Dr. Darin Detwiler, a nationally recognized food safety advocate, professor, and policy advocate who did not want his face on camera, said the Class I designation suggests the issue is more than routine paperwork. “It’s not like a paperwork thing; you know someone made the decision. This does not have to be reinspected at the border,” Detwiler said.
Detwiler also questioned how the recall was characterized, given that no contaminant was specified. “I find this curious because it's kind of like saying, hey, this is a paperwork problem; this is a bureaucratic problem. We forgot to do this, we missed this inspection, and we have no indication that there’s any problem, but we’re going to give it the highest classification of risk,” he said.
It was not immediately clear which retailers sold the beef. The distributor did not respond to a request for comment.
ALSO| Could the Flock camera debate influence the race for Texas governor?
The recall comes amid heightened attention on
foreign beef imports
. Last Friday, President Trump announced on Truth Social a plan to allow up to 300,000 pounds of foreign beef over the next 90 days to be sold at 25 percent less than current market prices.
Detwiler pointed to the timing of the announcement and the recall.
“This is where we get political, 24-48 hours about the administration approving meat coming from Argentina at a time that there’s a major recall of some 30000 pounds of meat because of failure to inspect it,” he said.
On Monday, Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico released a statement criticizing the plan, saying, “D.C. politicians are flooding the market with foreign beef and making it harder for them to get by. This is a political stunt that will only boost foreign competitors and make life harder for Texas cattlemen.” I reached out to Republican candidate Ken Paxton's campaign but did not get a response.
Since Trump’s announcement, Detwiler said, online discussion has fueled confusion about what is happening with beef imports and the recall.
“I don’t want to say it’s the imagination of the internet. What I want to say is it's amazing how we have all these kinds of conflicting pieces of information coming together right now at a time where there is this recall of the meat from Argentina,” he said.
A request for comment was also sent to the campaign for the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate, but no response was received.

不同观点：
• **RSS/开放网页更稳健**：可通过 RSS、OPML、公开 blogroll 建立订阅与推荐网络，避免依赖 Bluesky 的 Jetstream/API；Feedland 等还能展示“谁订阅了谁”。  
• **肯定 Bluesky 的开放数据模式**：Bluesky 不限制 AI 或其他程序抓取公开内容，仅统一进行限流，被认为在反 AI 氛围浓厚的社区中尤其难得。  
• **怀疑 ATProto 的实际创新**：有人质疑它是否真正去中心化、为何优于 Mastodon、Matrix 或 Scuttlebutt，并认为最终决定性因素仍是网络效应和注意力。  
• **反对技术包装和复杂化**：批评 ATProto 用大量 JSON、服务层和术语包装本可由网页索引、语义 HTML 等标准解决的问题，结果只是“更复杂的 Twitter”。  
• **现实主义立场**：去中心化的难点不在技术，而在内容质量、成本和用户体验；若不能低成本、易部署且提供有价值内容，就难以普及。社交平台关闭 API 也有商业止损和广告变现的现实原因。  
• **维护传统开放 Web**：社交媒体虽形成围墙花园，但整个 Web 仍可通过自建网站保持开放，不必把希望寄托于单一协议。  
• **质疑其正当性**：有人认为公开数据可被复制是事实，但并不代表平台“应当”支持这种功能，原文对企业限制数据的态度过于理所当然。

In 2007, Tim Berners Lee write the essay
The Giant Global Graph
. Quote:
There are cries from the heart .. for my friendship, that relationship to another person, to transcend documents and sites. ..Then any other site or program can use that information.
It seems appropriate as
X is sending cease-and-desist letters to Nitter
to remember TBL's essay. Nitter is - was - a simple frontend to X which allows users to view tweets without logging in. Even that small use of proxying to the pages is enough to receive threats of legal action.
Twitter's API in 2007 was famously open, which meant thousands of developers building clients, tools, and analytics for free. So, what happened? Why was it pulled? Simple: the network won. The developers stopped being an asset, and the API progressively closed. Rate limits, pricing tiers, login requirements, then technical blocks on the workarounds, and now letters from lawyers. source code

The web doesn't historically work that way. The web is a few dozen companies, each holding a filing cabinet, each with a receptionist posted out front. He'll read you one file at a time, but only files you can name, as fast as he cares to read, and as long as his boss allows.

Even the right questions come back in the wrong shape.

You can't join across "cabinets".
The interesting questions are almost always cross-service: this person's posts against that person's photos against a third service's reviews. Two receptionists in two buildings can't cross-reference anything, and neither can you.

• **怀疑 ATProto 的实际创新**：有人质疑它是否真正去中心化、为何优于 Mastodon、Matrix 或 Scuttlebutt，并认为最终决定性因素仍是网络效应和注意力。
